# standarnav (@standarx/nav)

> Spatial navigation for the web: d-pad, gamepad sticks, TV remotes and arrow keys drive real DOM focus, declared in data attributes. Headless TypeScript, zero runtime dependencies, ESM only. Unreleased: nothing is on npm yet, and the `data-snav-*` names are not frozen before v1.

This file is for an assistant helping someone use the package. The facts below are read from the source at the commit that published this file; when they disagree with the linked documents, the documents are newer.

## What the package is, and is not

- It moves the browser's real focus (`element.focus()`, `document.activeElement`). There is no virtual cursor and no focus registry.
- It ships **no component, no stylesheet and no widget**. A slider, a picker, a listbox or a dropdown is the application's markup; the package gives it the input grammar. Recipes for those controls live in the playground, linked below, and are meant to be copied.
- One instance per document, never a global: `createInputSystem(...)` returns a system with `destroy()`. Options are read once at construction; to change a mode or a plugin option, destroy and rebuild. The only things adjustable live are the gamepad plugin's `setMapping` and `assign`.
- Throws without a `document` (server render). Construct it in an effect or after mount.

## Entry points

Ten entry points in `package.json` `exports`; the root deliberately does not re-export the engines, so a consumer pays only for what it imports.

- `@standarx/nav` — `createInputSystem`, `pushEngageScope`, `createIntentBus`, `createIntentEvent`, `resolveKeyIntent`, `isTextEntryTarget`, `isIntentAllowedInTextEntry`, modality helpers (`getInputModality`, `setInputModality`, `trackInputModality`, `isFocusVisible`, `isFocusVisibleModality`, `MODALITY_ATTRIBUTE`), focusability primitives (`FOCUSABLE_SELECTOR`, `focusElement`, `getFocusables`, `isFocusable`, `isTabbable`), and the types.
- `@standarx/nav/spatial` — `spatialPlugin(options)`: the engine that turns `moveUp/Down/Left/Right` into a focus move. Without it, arrow keys and d-pads produce intents and nothing moves.
- `@standarx/nav/gamepad` — `gamepadPlugin(options)`: polls `navigator.getGamepads`, standard mapping, dead zones, repeat, rumble.
- `@standarx/nav/focus-ring` — `focusRingPlugin(options)`: one overlay element that follows `focusin`, painted inline, styled through six custom properties.
- `@standarx/nav/keyboard` — `keyboardPlugin({ layout, ... })`: an on-screen keyboard whose keys are real buttons the engine navigates.
- `@standarx/nav/keyboard/qwerty`, `/keyboard/azerty`, `/keyboard/alphabetic` — layout data only (`qwerty`, `azerty`, `alphabetic` exports). Import one; nothing registers itself.
- `@standarx/nav/react` — `NavProvider`, `useIntent`, `useInputSystem`, `useIntentScopeHost`, `useInputModality`, `NavDocumentProvider`. React 18.3+ is an optional peer.
- `@standarx/nav/debug` — `explainMove(origin, direction, { root?, score? })` returns the scored candidates and the winner of a move; `scanNativeSelects(root)` lists the closed native `<select>`s a television cannot navigate.

## Minimal setup

```ts
import { createInputSystem } from "@standarx/nav";
import { spatialPlugin } from "@standarx/nav/spatial";
import { gamepadPlugin } from "@standarx/nav/gamepad";
import { focusRingPlugin } from "@standarx/nav/focus-ring";

const input = createInputSystem({
  plugins: [spatialPlugin({ mode: "app" }), gamepadPlugin(), focusRingPlugin()],
});
// later: input.destroy();
```

`mode: "app"` is what makes arrow keys move across the page. The default, `"composite"`, leaves keyboard arrows to the page's own composite widgets (APG-strict) and only a gamepad crosses the page. A television, a kiosk or a dashboard wants `"app"`.

`createInputSystem` options: `doc`, `plugins`, `keymap` (`{ keys: { [event.key]: intent | null }, keyCodes: { [event.keyCode]: intent | null } }`; `null` disables a default row and lets the browser's native behaviour survive), `allowVerticalInText` (off by default).

The system: `pushScope(handler, { trapped?, base? })` returns a dispose; `emit(init)`; `onIntent(listener)`; `onModalityChange(listener)`; `pause()`; `resume()`; `destroy()`; `modality`.

## Markup contract (read by the engine)

| Attribute | On | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `data-snav="container"` | any element | declares a navigation container; moves are scored inside it first, nested containers count as one candidate |
| `data-snav-enter` | a container | `last` (default; falls back to `nearest`), `first`, `nearest` |
| `data-snav-wrap` | a container | `x`, `y`, `both`, or bare |
| `data-snav-block` | a container | directions separated by spaces, or bare for all |
| `data-snav-trap` | a container | bare; a move never leaves it |
| `data-snav-scroll` | a container | `center` |
| `data-snav-ignore` | any element | bare; not a candidate |
| `data-snav-up` / `-down` / `-left` / `-right` | a focusable | a CSS selector; that direction goes to the first match in the document before any geometry |

Written by the engine, for styling: `data-snav-focused` (the focused element), `data-snav-active` (every container on the path to it), `data-snav-input` on `<html>` (`keyboard`, `pointer`, `touch`, `gamepad`), `data-snav-focus-ring` (the ring overlay), `data-snav-editing` (the field the on-screen keyboard is open on), `data-snav-keyboard` (the keyboard box, valued with the layout id), `data-snav-keyboard-row`, `data-snav-keyboard-preview`, `data-snav-keyboard-caret`.

Focusable means the platform's own rule: `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `button`, `a[href]`, `area[href]`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, `audio[controls]`, `video[controls]`, `summary`, `[contenteditable]`, `[tabindex]`, minus `disabled`, hidden and `inert`. A clickable `div` needs `tabindex="0"`. `aria-hidden` and `aria-disabled` elements stay candidates on purpose. An element with a zero width or height is dropped; `opacity: 0` is not. Shadow roots are not traversed in v0.

## Intents and where they come from

`NavigationIntent`: `moveUp`, `moveDown`, `moveLeft`, `moveRight`, `select`, `secondary`, `back`, `contextMenu`, `tabNext`, `tabPrev`, `pageUp`, `pageDown`, `home`, `end`, `scrollX`, `scrollY`. An `IntentEvent` carries `intent`, `source` (`keyboard`, `gamepad`, `remote`), `repeat`, `value` (-1..1, analogue intents only), `originalEvent`, `defaultPrevented`, `preventDefault()`.

Default keymap: arrows → moves; Enter and Space → `select`; Escape → `back`; Tab → `tabNext`, Shift+Tab → `tabPrev`; PageUp/PageDown/Home/End; ContextMenu and Shift+F10 → `contextMenu`. TV remotes: `GoBack`, `BrowserBack`, `Exit` → `back`; `ChannelUp`/`ChannelDown` → `pageUp`/`pageDown`; keyCodes 461 (webOS Back), 10009 (Tizen Return), 10182 (Tizen Exit), 427/428 (channel). Anything with Ctrl, Alt or Meta produces nothing. Shift+arrow produces nothing (it is the range-extend gesture). Left/right are physical and never mirrored for RTL.

Gamepad standard mapping: button 0 (A/Cross) → `select`, 1 (B/Circle) → `back`, 2 (X/Square) → `secondary`, 3 (Y/Triangle) → `contextMenu`, 4/5 (LB/RB) → `tabPrev`/`tabNext`, 6/7 (LT/RT) → `pageUp`/`pageDown`, 9 (Start) → `contextMenu`, 12–15 (d-pad) → moves, left stick → moves through four sticky sectors, right stick → `scrollX`/`scrollY`. `swapNintendoConfirm` puts confirm on the glyph instead of the position.

## Scopes: how an application handles an intent

```ts
const dispose = input.pushScope((event) => {
  if (event.intent !== "back") return false; // not mine, keep walking
  closeDialog();
  return true; // consumed
}, { trapped: true });
```

- The top scope is asked first; returning `true` ends the walk and the system calls `preventDefault()` on the key that carried the intent, in the capture phase.
- `trapped: true` swallows every intent it does not handle, except `back`, `tabNext` and `tabPrev`, which always escape (a dialog must be leavable; Tab is the focus trap's business).
- `base: true` is asked even through a trap. The spatial engine is a base scope: a trapped dialog still gets d-pad movement inside it. The confinement comes from `data-snav-trap` on the dialog's container, not from the scope.
- An unclaimed `select` from a gamepad or remote clicks the focused element, so A works on a button, a checkbox or a link with no code. It never does that for a keyboard source (the browser already clicks), never on repeat, and never on a text-entry target. Inside a trapped scope nothing clicks the focused element for you: the scope has to call `.click()` itself.
- `spatialPlugin` also exposes `move(direction)`, `focus(elementOrSelector)`, `focusFirst(container?)`, `onWillMove(listener)` (call `event.preventDefault()` to veto), `onBoundsHit(listener)`.

## Engage mode: controls that hold a value

A gamepad cannot drag. `pushEngageScope(host, { onAdjust(intent, event), onRelease?(committed) })` takes hold of a control: the four moves plus `pageUp`, `pageDown`, `home`, `end` become adjustments, `select` releases with `committed = true`, `back` releases with `committed = false` (restore the entry value). The returned dispose detaches silently and does not call `onRelease`. Recipes for a slider, a stepper, a wheel picker, a listbox, a splitter and a native `<select>` are in `playground/widgets.ts` and are driven by the browser tests.

Constraints to know before writing one:

- A control must not be a text-entry target. `<input type="number">` is one, so `select` never reaches it and it cannot be engaged; the stepper recipe uses a `<button>` that owns the value. `<input type="range">` is fine.
- Enter engage through a scope that claims `select` while the control is focused, not through a click handler: that is the one route identical for a pad, a remote and a keyboard.
- Engage returns `tabNext` to the layer beneath, so a user can Tab out of a held control; the recipe releases on `focusout` and redoes the commit-or-restore itself.
- Backspace as "let go" is bound to the held control, not to the keymap: `back` is allowed inside a text field, so a global Backspace row would erase a character and leave the field at once.

## Pitfalls

- **Text fields are dead ends by design.** Inside `input`, `textarea`, `[contenteditable]`, `role="textbox"` or `role="searchbox"` only `back`, `tabNext`, `tabPrev` and `contextMenu` reach a scope. Left and right never do. `allowVerticalInText: true` lets `moveUp`, `moveDown`, `pageUp` and `pageDown` out, which is what a form on a television needs; leave it off for a `textarea`-heavy page.
- **A native `<select>` cannot be navigated on a television.** Closed, it opens a platform popup outside the document; the engine loses the focus into it, and on a desktop the bug is invisible because the browser drives its own popup. `scanNativeSelects` in `/debug` finds them. The recipe: claim `select` while the `<select>` is focused (that also suppresses Enter and Space, which would open the popup), open a `data-snav="container" data-snav-trap` list of real buttons built from its `<option>`s, click the focused option yourself, restore focus to the `<select>` on close, intercept `mousedown` (the popup opens on the press) and Alt+ArrowDown (a modifier never reaches the keymap). `multiple` and `size > 1` render in the document and need nothing.
- **`gamepadPlugin().assign(padIndex, route)` is a total override, not a filter.** With a route set, every intent from that pad goes to the route and never to the shared stack; an intent the route does not re-emit is dropped.
- **Nothing hot-swaps.** `mode`, `pointerFollowsFocus`, `allowVerticalInText` and every plugin option are read at construction. Rebuild the system to change them.
- **React: hoist or memoise the plugins.** `NavProvider` compares the `plugins` list element by element; `plugins={[gamepadPlugin()]}` is a new instance every render and rebuilds the whole system. `useInputSystem()` is `null` until the provider's effect has run and on the server; `useIntent` copes with that itself.
- **Hidden lists and CSS specificity.** A recipe that hides its list with the `hidden` attribute loses to any bare `display` rule on the same element, because `[hidden] { display: none }` has class specificity. Write the rule as `.list:not([hidden]) { display: grid }`.
- **No `navigator.getGamepads`, no pad.** The gamepad plugin registers nothing when the API is absent (Playwright's WebKit, some television runtimes) rather than throwing inside `createInputSystem`.
- **`composite` on a laptop looks like nothing happening.** Arrow keys are handed to the page; only Tab and a pad move. Use `mode: "app"` when the whole page is the composite.
- **`pointerFollowsFocus`** is on in `app` and off in `composite`: under `app` a hover focuses what it crosses, so a mouse and a pad do not fight over two cursors.

## Focus ring and on-screen keyboard

- Focus ring: `focusRingPlugin({ offset?, duration? })`, `refresh()` after a layout change it cannot see. Custom properties, inherited by the overlay: `--snav-focus-ring-z-index` (1700), `--snav-focus-ring-width` (3px), `--snav-focus-ring-color` (#1a73e8), `--snav-focus-ring-offset` (2), `--snav-focus-ring-duration` (260 ms, 150 under reduced motion), `--snav-focus-ring-easing`. A custom property of the wrong type makes the ring compute to nothing with no error. `box-shadow` is suppressed under `forced-colors: active`.
- On-screen keyboard: `keyboardPlugin({ layout, container?, openOn? })` with `openOn` one of `activate` (default: a click on the field or a `select` on it from any device; never a focus alone), `focus`, `gamepad`, `manual`. Methods `open(field)`, `close()`, `isOpen()`, `target()`. Insertion goes through `beforeinput`, the mutation, then `input`, so a mask can refuse a keystroke by cancelling `beforeinput`. `back` closes and keeps what was typed. `contenteditable` is refused. A layout is `{ id, languages, layers: { [name]: rows }, initialLayer }` where a row is a string (one key per character) or an array of `{ label, value?, action?, shift?, span?, layer? }` with `action` one of `backspace`, `space`, `enter`, `shift`, `layer`, `close`.

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/README.md): install, usage, the attribute tables, React, how a move is decided, browser support.
- [Specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/docs/specification.md): the problem, the non-goals, the user contract and the numbered requirements.
- [Roadmap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/ROADMAP.md): what is open before the first publication, and what v1 freezes.
- [Decision records index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/docs/adr/README.md): every ADR with what it decides.
- [ADR-0007 navigation modes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/docs/adr/0007-navigation-modes.md): `composite` versus `app`.
- [ADR-0021 native select on television](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/docs/adr/0021-native-select-on-television.md): why the popup is unreachable and what replaces it.
- [ADR-0022 virtual keyboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/docs/adr/0022-virtual-keyboard.md): layouts, insertion, what closes it.
- [Playground](https://standarx-miralabs-tech.github.io/standarnav/): the fixture page, driven by keyboard and gamepad, with a device panel for every option.
- [Engage and select recipes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/playground/widgets.ts): `attachEngageable`, `attachSlider`, `attachStepper`, `attachWheelPicker`, `attachListbox`, `attachNativeSelect`, `attachSplitter`.

## Source

- [Input system](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/src/input-system.ts): `createInputSystem`, the keydown listener, `activateFocused`.

- [Gamepad engine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/src/gamepad/gamepad.ts): options, `setMapping`, `assign`, `rumble`.

- [On-screen keyboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StandarX-miralabs-tech/standarnav/main/src/keyboard/keyboard.ts): `KeyboardLayout`, `KeyboardKey`, `openOn`.
